style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">13. <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesDisclosureTextBlock" id="f-1061" continuedAt="f-1061-1" escape="true">Commitments and Contingencies</ix:nonNumeric></span></div><ix:continuation id="f-1061-1" continuedAt="f-1061-2"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Legal Proceedings</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">From time to time, the Company may face legal claims or actions in the normal course of business. Except as disclosed below, the Company is not currently a party to any material litigation.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Xtampza ER Litigation </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On March 24, 2015, Purdue sued the Company in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware asserting infringement of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="patent" contextRef="c-231" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyPatentsAllegedlyInfringedNumber" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1062">three</ix:nonFraction> of Purdue&#8217;s Orange Book-listed patents (Patent Nos. 7,674,799, 7,674,800, and 7,683,072) and a non-Orange Book-listed patent (Patent No. 8,652,497). The lawsuit was initiated in response to the Company filing the New Drug Application (&#8220;NDA&#8221;) for Xtampza ER as a 505(b)(2) application referencing data from Purdue&#8217;s OxyContin NDA, and under the Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984, triggered a stay of up to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-231" name="coll:LossContingencyStayPeriodBeforeFinalFederalDrugAdministrationApprovalCanBeIssuedIfPatentInfringementLitigationElected" format="ixt-sec:durmonth" id="f-1063">30</ix:nonNumeric> months before the FDA could issue a final approval for Xtampza ER, unless the stay was earlier terminated.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Delaware court transferred the case to the District of Massachusetts. After the Company filed a partial motion for judgment on the pleadings relating to the Orange Book-listed patents, the District Court of Massachusetts ordered judgment in the Company&#8217;s favor on those <ix:nonFraction unitRef="patent" contextRef="c-232" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyPatentsAllegedlyInfringedNumber" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1064">three</ix:nonFraction> patents, and dismissed the claims which lifted the <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-232" name="coll:LossContingencyStayPeriodBeforeFinalFederalDrugAdministrationApprovalCanBeIssuedIfPatentInfringementLitigationElected" format="ixt-sec:durmonth" id="f-1065">30</ix:nonNumeric>-month stay of FDA approval. Following this judgment, the Company obtained final approval for Xtampza ER and launched commercially. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Purdue subsequently filed <ix:nonFraction unitRef="lawsuit" contextRef="c-233" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyNewClaimsFiledNumber" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1066">two</ix:nonFraction> follow-on lawsuits asserting infringement of <ix:nonFraction unitRef="patent" contextRef="c-233" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyPatentsAllegedlyInfringedNumber" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1067">two</ix:nonFraction> patents that had been late-listed in the Orange Book and, therefore, could not trigger any stay of FDA approval: Purdue asserted infringement of Patent No. 9,073,933 in November 2015 and Patent No. 9,522,919 in April 2017. In addition, Purdue invoked <ix:nonFraction unitRef="patent" contextRef="c-233" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyPatentsAllegedlyInfringedNumber" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1068">two</ix:nonFraction> non-Orange Book-listed patents, filing suit in June 2016 asserting infringement of Patent No. 9,155,717 and in September 2017, asserting infringement of Patent No. 9,693,961.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On March 13, 2018, the Company filed a Petition for Post-Grant Review (&#8220;PGR&#8221;) of the &#700;961 patent with the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (&#8220;PTAB&#8221;). The PGR argued that the &#700;961 patent is invalid. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On November 21, 2017, the Court issued its claim construction ruling, construing certain claims of the &#700;933, &#700;497, and &#700;717 patents. The Court issued an order on September 28, 2018, in which it ruled that the Xtampza ER formulation does not infringe the &#700;497 and &#700;717 patents. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On September 15, 2019, Purdue commenced chapter 11 bankruptcy proceedings in the United States Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York. Later in September 2019, Purdue gave the District Court of Massachusetts, as well as the PTAB, notice of its bankruptcy filing and sought the imposition of an automatic stay of proceedings. Both the Court and the PTAB granted Purdue&#8217;s requests to stay the pending matters. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On September 1, 2020, the Bankruptcy Court entered an Order, lifting the automatic stays in both the District of Massachusetts and PTAB proceedings. On September 11, 2020, Purdue filed a motion to terminate the PTAB action on the basis that those proceedings had gone beyond the <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-234" name="coll:StatutoryPeriodOfProceedings" format="ixt-sec:durmonth" id="f-1069">18</ix:nonNumeric>-month statutory period. On November 19, 2021, the PTAB: (i) denied Purdue&#8217;s motion to terminate the PGR; and (ii) issued its Final Written Decision, finding that the asserted claims of the &#700;961 patent were invalid for lack of written description and anticipation. Purdue appealed the decision to Federal Circuit, which issued its decision on November 21, 2023, affirming the authority of the PTAB to issue its Final Written Decision and upholding the PTAB&#8217;s finding of invalidity relative to the &#8217;961 patent.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On April 2, 2021, the Court granted Purdue&#8217;s Motion to Lift the Stay in the District of Massachusetts that was entered following Purdue&#8217;s Notice of Bankruptcy. As the internal reporting is based on the consolidated results, the Company has identified <ix:nonFraction unitRef="segment" contextRef="c-1" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:NumberOfOperatingSegments" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1530"><ix:nonFraction unitRef="segment" contextRef="c-1" decimals="INF" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" scale="0" id="f-1531">one</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction> operating and reportable segment and the measure of segment profit or loss is consolidated net income. The significant segment expenses for functional areas exclude stock-based compensation and certain other segment expenses, and are reported for </span></div></ix:continuation><div style="height:45pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;text-align:center"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">F-47</span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline"><a style="color:#0000ff;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;text-decoration:underline" href="#idad25bcb385e41bf966f247faa2ba0c6_7">Table of Contents</a></span></div></div><ix:continuation id="f-1529-2"><div style="margin-bottom:10pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">the following functional areas: corporate, medical, technical operations, and commercial. The corporate functional area includes operating expenses related to finance, legal, business development, and other administrative activities, excluding stock-based compensation and other segment expenses (&#8220;Corporate Expenses&#8221;). The medical functional area includes operating expenses related to medical affairs, regulatory, pharmacovigilance and other medical-related activities, excluding stock-based compensation and other segment expenses (&#8220;Medical Expenses&#8221;). The technical operations functional area includes non-inventoriable operating expenses related to supply chain, product quality, information technology and other technical activities, excluding stock-based compensation and other segment expenses (&#8220;Technical Operations Expenses&#8221;). The commercial function includes operating expenses related to sales, marketing, market access, and other commercial activities, excluding stock-based compensation and other segment expenses (&#8220;Commercial Expenses&#8221;). Stock compensation is a significant segment expense and other segment expenses are included in Other segment items or separately stated in the table below. </span></div><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="c-1"
